objects.description: Intrinsic timer node used by the timing system. Each Timer participates in a per-component doubly linked list (indexed by componentOffset), with next/prev storing indices into the global timers array. The components array tracks remaining ticks per resolution bucket. overshootMs tracks accumulated overshoot; nextOriginalMs is reserved for potential repeat timers but is not used in this header.

functions.name: cb
functions.description: Prints a message when a timer triggers. Intended as a sample callback; real callbacks are set via setTimeout_.
requirements: No inputs or state requirements.
Intended for demonstration/testing; production code should set its own callback via setTimeout_.

functions.name: init
functions.description: Initializes the timer subsystem. Resets the free timer stack and clears all per-component list heads.
requirements: Must be called before allocateTimer, setTimeout_, addTimerToList, tick, or any list manipulation functions.
Calling init after timers have been allocated or lists populated will reset internal state and invalidate existing timers.

functions.name: allocateTimer
functions.description: Obtains a free timer ID from the freeTimers stack and returns it.
requirements: init must have been called to populate the free timer stack.
There must be at least one free timer available; otherwise behavior is undefined (no bounds checks).
Each returned timer ID must later be returned via freeTimer exactly once before being reallocated again.

functions.name: freeTimer
functions.description: Returns a timer ID to the free timer stack for reuse.
requirements: The timer must have been previously returned by allocateTimer and not yet freed.
The timer should not still be linked in any component list when freed (unlink first).
Do not free the same timer more than once.

functions.name: divideComponents
functions.signature: unsigned int divideComponents(unsigned int components[5], unsigned int *biggestSetComponent, unsigned int ms);
functions.description: Decomposes a timeout in milliseconds into counts of five timer components with granularities {10,50,100,500,1000} ms. Fills components with the number of ticks for each granularity and returns the overshoot in milliseconds needed to round up to the next 10 ms tick.
requirements: components must point to a writable array of at least 5 unsigned ints and should be zero-initialized before the call (function only writes indices it divides and may increment components[0]).
biggestSetComponent must be a valid pointer to an unsigned int and should be initialized to 0 before the call; it will be updated to the highest component index that was set.
ms may be any unsigned int; non-multiples of 10 will cause components[0] to be incremented and an overshoot (10 - ms % 10) to be returned.

functions.name: addTimerToList
functions.signature: void addTimerToList(unsigned int timer, unsigned int componentOffset);
functions.description: Inserts a timer into the head of the per-component doubly linked list identified by componentOffset and records that membership in the timer.
requirements: timer must be a valid timer ID (e.g., from allocateTimer) and not currently linked in any list.
componentOffset must be in the range [0, 4], corresponding to the five component lists.
Caller must ensure timer->prev/next linkage will not corrupt existing lists (i.e., do not add the same timer twice).

functions.name: removeTimerFromList
functions.signature: unsigned int removeTimerFromList(unsigned int timer, unsigned int componentOffset);
functions.description: Unlinks a timer from the specified per-component list. Returns the next timer in that list after the removed node, or UINT_MAX if none.
requirements: timer must currently be linked in the list identified by componentOffset.
componentOffset must be in the range [0, 4].
If the timer is not in the specified list, list integrity can be corrupted.
Return value should be checked for UINT_MAX to detect end-of-list.

functions.name: moveTimerToList
functions.signature: unsigned int moveTimerToList(unsigned int timer, unsigned int newComponentOffset);
functions.description: Moves a timer from its current per-component list to another specified list. Returns the next timer in the original list after the moved node, or UINT_MAX if none.
requirements: timer must currently be linked in some component list; its current list is taken from timers[timer].componentOffset.
newComponentOffset must be in the range [0, 4].
Caller should use the return value to continue iteration safely when iterating the original list.

functions.name: tick
functions.description: Advances the timers in the specified component list by one tick for that granularity, moving timers to more precise lists or invoking their callbacks when all components reach zero.
requirements: componentOffset must be in the range [0, 4]; it should correspond to a system tick of componentMultiplierMs[componentOffset] milliseconds.
Callbacks invoked via timerCallbacks[timer]() must not modify the timer lists during execution (per in-code comment).
tick should be called by a system timer at the cadence matching the component’s granularity for correct scheduling.

functions.name: setTimeout_
functions.signature: unsigned int setTimeout_(void (*cb)(), unsigned int ms);
functions.description: Schedules a one-shot timer to invoke the provided callback after approximately ms milliseconds, rounded up to the next 10 ms tick. Returns the allocated timer ID.
requirements: init must have been called before use to initialize free timers and list heads.
cb must be a valid non-null function pointer taking no arguments; if null, calling it will cause a crash.
There must be a free timer available; otherwise behavior is undefined.
The returned timer is linked into an internal list and must be cleared with clearTimeout_ if cancellation is needed before it fires.

functions.name: clearTimeout_
functions.description: Cancels a scheduled timer by unlinking it from its current list and returning it to the free timer pool.
requirements: timer must be a valid timer ID currently linked in a component list created by setTimeout_ or addTimerToList.
Do not pass a timer that has already been freed; doing so will corrupt the free stack.
Should not be called from within a tick callback that might be iterating the same list (list modification is not supported during callback execution).
